title: Stopping state triggers a finish step
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\Gamma$ and $S$ be types, let $e$ be an injection from the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$, let $M$ be a Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, alphabet $\Gamma$, and state set $S$, and let $\mathrm{stopAt}:S\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. For any finite input $x$ over $\Gamma$, any configuration $c$ of $M$ on $x$, any state $s\in S$ with $\mathrm{stopAt}(s)=\mathrm{true}$, any clock-tape contents $ct:\mathbb Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\Gamma)$, and any clock-head position $cp\in\mathbb Z$, one step of the clocked machine from the configuration with state $(s,\mathrm{run})$, body configuration $c$, and clock data $ct,cp$ yields the configuration with state $\mathrm{finish}(s)$ and the same body configuration and clock data.
hypotheses_covered: $e$ is an injection from the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$
$M$ is a Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, alphabet $\Gamma$, and state set $S$
